resources.string: The console\'s built-in storage chip: details and backups
This console has no built-in eMMC that andr36oid can switch on.
The built-in eMMC is switched off. Switch on Kernel Tweaks > Built-in eMMC storage, then restart the console.
The eMMC\'s details couldn\'t be read.
Switched on, but no eMMC answered. This console may not have one, or the kernel left it off because something else uses its pins. A problem report has the details.
Worn out: past its rated life
Spare blocks almost gone: back it up soon
Takes about 16 seconds and only reads
The speed test couldn\'t read the eMMC.
Copies the eMMC, or a part of it, to image files in the folder \"eMMC backup\" on the storage you pick. The eMMC is only read: the system on it stays as it is.
%1$s: all partitions, the partition table and the boot areas, to put it back exactly as it is
%1$s go to the folder \"eMMC backup\" on %2$s. The console stays awake until it\'s done.
That storage uses FAT32, which takes files up to 4 GB, so the image is split into numbered pieces (.001, .002…). Join them on a computer before using the image.
%1$s needs %2$s free for this, it has %3$s.
What was copied so far stays in the folder, but it\'s not a complete image.
Stopped. %2$s on %1$s holds an incomplete copy.
The eMMC couldn\'t be read to the end. %2$s on %1$s holds an incomplete copy.
Put andr36oid on the built-in eMMC, so the console starts without the SD card
andr36oid only installs onto the eMMC when it runs from the SD card.
andr36oid is running from the built-in eMMC. To change the installation or put the stock system back, start from the andr36oid SD card.
The test worked: andr36oid started from the eMMC.\n\nRestart now. The console starts from the SD card again, where the installation finishes. Leave the SD card in.
Step 0: Back up the stock eMMC
Step 1: Prove the SD card\'s loader
Step 2: Prove andr36oid on the eMMC
Step 3: Put the loader on the eMMC
The installer couldn\'t look at the console.
No built-in eMMC found. Switch it on in Kernel Tweaks > Built-in eMMC storage and restart.
Big enough for andr36oid (8 GB or more)
The stock system will be gone

Everything on the built-in eMMC is replaced: the system the console came with, its games and its settings. A full copy is made first and you can put it back from here, but only with this SD card and only while the console still starts.

Writing the loader that starts the console is the most dangerous thing you can do to it. If it goes wrong, the console may not switch on at all, and nothing andr36oid can do will help.\n\nConsoles whose eMMC and memory are one chip (eMCP) are the worst: they have no easy way to force them into recovery. Getting them back can mean opening the case and soldering, or may not be possible.

This is experimental. Nobody can promise it works on your console, and nobody can fix it for you if it doesn\'t.\n\nThe partition sizes are fixed now. Later andr36oid versions can only be put on the eMMC if they fit.
How the eMMC is split up
system and vendor get room to grow for later versions, your apps and data get the rest.
All %1$s of the eMMC (sectors 0-%2$d) and its two boot areas are read, read again to compare, copied to %3$s, and read back. Nothing is written to the eMMC.
eMMC sectors 64-32767 (the stock loader, 16 MiB) are blanked. Then you restart: the console has to start from the SD card\'s loader on its own.

A new partition table (eMMC sectors 0-33 and %1$d-%2$d); BOOT, system and vendor copied from the SD card; the start of metadata, misc, cache and userdata blanked:\n%3$sThen andr36oid starts from the eMMC once, as a test.
The SD card\'s sectors 64-32767 (its loader) are copied to the eMMC, after one more warning.

Every write is read back and compared. If anything doesn\'t match, the installer stops and writes nothing more. Steps 1 and 2 are each proven by a restart before the next one. Step 3 is the only write that can\'t be tried out first.
The stock eMMC is backed up. Next is step 1: its loader is blanked, then you restart.
Step 1 passed: the console started from the SD card\'s loader on its own.\n\nNext is step 2: andr36oid is copied to the eMMC (a few minutes), then it starts from there once.
Step 2 passed: andr36oid started from the eMMC.\n\nNext is step 3: the loader goes onto the eMMC.

The eMMC\'s loader is blank. Restart now: the console has to start from the SD card\'s loader on its own, and this page opens again.\n\nIf it doesn\'t come back: hold power for 7 seconds and switch it on again. If it still doesn\'t start, this console needs its stock loader. The backup is in %1$s on this SD card.

andr36oid is on the eMMC. Restart now: it starts from the eMMC once, as a test. Its first start sets things up and takes a few minutes. When it says the test worked, restart again.\n\nIf it hangs: hold power for 7 seconds and switch it on again. It then starts from the SD card as usual, and this page says what happened.
Shut the console down, take the SD card out once it is off, then switch it on: andr36oid now starts from the eMMC.\n\nWith an andr36oid SD card in, the console starts from the card, as before.
Shut the console down, take the SD card out once it is off, then switch it on to use the stock system.

This writes the loader that starts the console onto the eMMC. Everything before this was tested. This is not: the loader has to read U-Boot from the eMMC, which the stock loader shows works on this board, but these exact bytes never ran from the eMMC.\n\nIf it fails, the console doesn\'t switch on any more, with or without an SD card.
It\'s my fault if this goes wrong
Hold A for 10 seconds. Letting go starts over.
The installer has no loader checksum from step 1.
andr36oid is installed on the eMMC. Without an SD card the console starts from the eMMC; with an andr36oid SD card in, it starts from the card.
Nothing more was written after this. Your stock eMMC is backed up in %1$s.\n\nPut the stock eMMC back, or leave it as it is?
Nothing was written to the eMMC.
%1$s was cut off before it finished (power lost?).
andr36oid didn\'t start from the eMMC in the test.
The installer stopped without saying how it went.

Copies this SD card\'s andr36oid to the eMMC: its BOOT files, system and vendor, and U-Boot if it changed. Apps, data and settings on the eMMC stay.\n\nKeep the console charging. If the update is cut off, the console starts from the SD card until you run it again.
Everything andr36oid wrote to the eMMC is replaced by the backup in %1$s. The backup is checked first, and the eMMC is compared with it afterwards. This takes a few minutes.
Step 0 only reads the eMMC. Nothing is written to it yet.
Write the loader to the eMMC

Installing on the eMMC takes a while: everything written is read back and compared with the original before the wizard moves on. That\'s deliberate. One bad write in the wrong place can leave the console unable to start at all, so each step has to be proven correct before the next one begins.
The backup is written back to the eMMC part by part. Then the whole eMMC is read back and compared with the backup, so you know it is exactly the stock eMMC again.
The new andr36oid is copied from the SD card to the eMMC one part at a time. Each part is read back and compared with the SD card before the next one starts.
Keep the console switched on and the SD card in until this is done.
